thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Canary cluster rwd-prod-canary reporting 99p latency spike + increased 5xx after recent deploy (deploy id: deploy-2026-03-15-1010). Pager routed to @eric-oncall. Auto-run diagnostics kicked off: <https://redwood.internal/alerts/2630456789>
eric-oncall: oncall here, looking at dashboards now. seeing 99p up ~2.5x vs baseline, tail latencies up and a small bump in 5xx. grabbing logs and rolling traces.
maya: saw kernel fallback alerts in logs ~10:11 UTC: "kernel selection fallback -> generic_cpu_kernel" repeated across a few hosts. sending snippet.
maya: ```
kernel: failed to allocate fast-path workspace, falling back to generic_cpu_kernel
runtime: kv-cache miss rate spike: 42% -> 86%
batcher: avg queue depth 12 -> 48
```
raj: batcher backlog + kv evictions = higher per-token cost and higher latency. looks like the new runtime change to session-affinity scheduling is causing imbalance on some GPU instances.
sylvia: concrete customer impact? CSMs seeing reports?
natalie: CSM Olivia reports two customers in EU saw degraded response times and a couple of transient 503s. raising a heads-up to account teams.
csm-olivia: Confirmed. Affects tenant ids: tenant-42 (search), tenant-84 (chat). Not huge error count but high tail latency for interactive flows. Customers are noticing.
eric-oncall: ok, priority: mitigate user impact first. Options: immediate rollback, flip feature flag kill-switch for session-affinity, or reduce canary traffic. Which is least blasty?
deploy-bot: rollback command available: `/deploy rollback deploy-2026-03-15-1010 --force` — requires approver. Feature flag toggle: `ff toggle canary-session-affinity off --env canary`.
raj: flipping FF is lowest-risk and fast; rollback is heavier and will impact more. flipping should route requests to previous scheduling code path.
sylvia: agree — flip FF + reduce canary traffic to 10% while we observe. if metrics don't improve, escalate rollback.
eric-oncall: doing it now. @deploy-bot flip.
deploy-bot: running: `ff toggle canary-session-affinity off --env canary`
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: feature flag `canary-session-affinity` set to `off` for canary scope.
backend-sre: I pushed a small throttle to canary traffic at the balancer (slice weight -> 10%). command: `balancer set-weight rwd-canary 0.1` executed.
eric-oncall: metrics: starting to see queue depth fall within 2 minutes. 99p moving toward baseline slowly. 5xx count stabilizing.
maya: kernel fallback logs dropping off on the previously noisy hosts. kv-miss rate trending down.
natalie: notifying affected customers: sent initial message with status and ETA for update (cc @csm-olivia).
csm-olivia: customers acknowledged and appreciate quick action.
eric-oncall: good. keeping this thread open for 30m observation. if tail doesn't return to baseline, we'll plan a full rollback. postmortem owner?
raj: I'll take postmortem. root hypothesis: scheduling change + session-affinity caused uneven load packing -> some machines saturated -> kernel allocation failures -> fallback -> slower execution path and batch thrashing. Need to validate with trace samples and heatmap.
sylvia: also want to check batching config change that shipped with the runtime patch; maybe batching thresholds interacted poorly with affinity.
maya: capturing `strace`-like sampling and runtime state dump from affected hosts now. attaching logs to alert: <https://redwood.internal/alerts/2630456789/logs>
backend-sre: none of the control-plane autoscale triggers fired because container-level memory looked fine; the problem was per-GPU allocation fragmentation. follow-up: add soft guardrails to detect kernel-fallback bursts and auto-fall back to older scheduler earlier.
eric-oncall: thanks — will keep monitoring. next steps: 1) raj to run deep postmortem and capture roll-forward plan, 2) backend-sre to add alert for kernel-fallback bursts, 3) maya to collect traces and kv cache heatmaps, 4) sylvia to validate batching thresholds.
raj: acknowledged. I'll start the postmortem doc and link it here.
eric-oncall: closing alert if no regression observed in next 30m. will hand off to eng-runtime for long-term fix.
deploy-bot: incident note: mitigation applied: feature-flag flipped, canary traffic weight reduced.
natalie: I logged customer impact and outreach actions in the incident tracker. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
eric-oncall: handing to eng-runtime for follow-up. Marking P1->P2 (customer impact limited, mitigated).
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated at 2026-03-15T10:20:00Z. Timeline and artifacts: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/2630456789>
raj: postmortem draft incoming.
